changelog.a10.credit_no_full_with_overdu: Two tightenings to the Repayment Credit tiers: ① full marks now go only to vendors whose «overdue >7 days ratio = 0», removing the lenient «≤10% also counts as full marks» tier; ② the tiers now match the official announcement — ≤20% → 80 points, 20–50% → 50 points, ≥50% → 0 points (previously ≤30% / 30–60% / >60%). Why: granting full marks at ≤10% was inherited from the finance-side definition and contradicted the principle that full marks mean paying on time. Note: full marks look at whether the overdue ratio is 0 — they do **not** require having no debt at all; a vendor whose entire balance is within terms and not overdue also gets full marks.
changelog.a11.summary: Tier boundaries made explicit: the 0-point tier always includes its boundary value (CR-20260814 A11)
changelog.a11.zero_tier_inclusive: For every indicator, the 0-point tier now includes its boundary value, so the published table leaves no doubt about which tier that value falls into: average daily Perfect Orders ≤100, Slot Compliance Rate ≤40%, New Rider Ratio ≤30%, overdue >7 days ratio ≥50%, blocked-account rate ≥15%, and D-3R% ≥3% (already inclusive). Why: previously a boundary value landed in either the 50-point or the 0-point tier depending on whether the tier used ≥ or >, which allowed two readings of the published table; assigning it to the 0-point tier throughout makes the tiers mutually exclusive and lets vendors self-assess straight from the table.
changelog.a11.reason: In the published tier table, every boundary value must have an unambiguous home, and it always belongs to the 0-point tier (management's definition, 2026-08-14).

indicator.orders.desc: The size of your operation: average daily Perfect Orders in the assessed period (total Perfect Orders in the period ÷ days in the period — calendar days for a month, 7 days for a week).
indicator.slot.desc: Whether you deliver the shifts you committed to: slots met each day of the month ÷ total target slots for the month (accumulated daily, not the average of weekly rates). A slot counts as met when attending riders reach the set proportion of the target; the shifts assessed are those in the target issued each week. Weekend and contest-period weighting affects only the full-time bonus amount — level assessment uses the actual compliance rate.
indicator.credit.desc: Share of debt overdue >7 days — the lower the better. Pay on time = full score; partners with no debt automatically score 100. Measured from weekly snapshots, averaged over the month. Amounts under dispute do not count as overdue (invoice disputes are decoupled from repayment).
indicator.d3r.desc: The share of orders a rider rejects, reassigns or reschedules — the lower the better.
indicator.newrider.desc: Measures recruiting quality: riders entirely new to the industry ÷ riders hired this month — how many of your new hires are new to the industry. A new rider is one entirely new to the DiDi platform (never in another DiDi rider program before joining the Vendor program), verified by CURP.
indicator.blocked_rider_rate.desc: The share of riders the platform blocks for non-compliant accounts (the rider does not match the registered ID): riders blocked this month ÷ riders completing orders this month — the lower the better. Zero blocks earns full marks.

rules.direct_c.intro: Integrity and compliance are the basis of our partnership. If any of the following occurs, the month's level is set directly to C (benefits are suspended at the same time and the warning process begins):
rules.direct_c.strike: Organising or causing rider strikes, work stoppages or other collective incidents
rules.direct_c.integrity: Breaching the platform's integrity standards: bribing platform staff, falsifying data and similar
rules.direct_c.other_major: Other serious incidents that cross the platform's red lines
rules.direct_c.vs_redline: Note: this section covers integrity and compliance, while the Debt Red Line covers payment discipline. They are two separate mechanisms, each determined independently.
rules.total_formula: Total points = Σ (indicator points × weight). Every indicator has 4 tiers: 100 / 80 / 50 / 0 points.
rules.credit.formula: Repayment Credit = points for the share overdue >7 days (averaged across the month's weekly snapshots). If that share is 0 you get full marks ({noDebt} points) — it does not require having no debt at all; debt entirely within terms also earns full marks.
rules.credit.formula_multi: Repayment Credit = {parts} (weekly snapshots, averaged within the month). No overdue debt = {noDebt} points.
rules.credit.overdue_ratio: Share overdue >7 days (debt more than 7 days overdue ÷ total debt)
rules.credit.bad_debt_ratio: Bad-debt share (debt more than 30 days overdue ÷ total debt)
rules.credit.appeal: Amounts under dispute do not count as overdue (invoice disputes are decoupled from repayment).
gate.s_scale_blocked: (The S scale threshold has been retired as of 2026-09) Total points meet the S line, but average daily Perfect Orders fall short of the threshold, so level A is awarded per the rules
rules.levels.s: Total points ≥ {sline} and {indicator} ≥ {gate} (same across the market)
rules.levels.note: The score lines for levels S, A and C are each set per city according to its stage of market development, and are recalibrated periodically as the market changes; every recalibration is published through official channels before it takes effect. The indicators assessed and the tier standards are the same across the market.
rules.redline.weekly: Weekly mark = debt overdue >7 days of ≥ {amount} that also makes up ≥ {ratio}% of total debt
rules.redline.trigger: Marked in ≥ {hits} weekly snapshots during the month and still marked in the month's final snapshot → the Red Line is triggered
rules.redline.action: Consequence: the month's cash incentive is forfeited (not paid, not paid retroactively, not offset against your debt); once settled, incentive eligibility resumes the following month
rules.redline.warning: Warning line: bad-debt balance ≥ credit limit, or Red Line status for {weeks} consecutive weeks → you enter a warning period
rules.redline.level_cap: In the month the Red Line is triggered, the level is capped at {level}
rules.redline.relation: Note: the level cap and the incentive forfeiture are not stacked as a double penalty — being capped at B already brings the cash incentive to zero, and "the month's incentive is forfeited" simply states that same consequence explicitly.
rules.flex.note: Flexible Adjustment: added to or subtracted from the weighted total of the six indicators, with a net cap of ±{n} points. The bonus and the penalty are different in nature, so they are defined and shown separately.
flex.activity.note: Activity bonus: the platform publishes the task list and the points for each task in advance (new-area pilots, weekly sprints and similar), and vendors earn them simply by taking part — fully transparent.
flex.penalty.note: Violation penalty: applies to misconduct determined after the fact. Every penalty must come with a reason that can be explained to the vendor and must be communicated promptly (how many points and why).
rules.flex.order: Order of calculation: weighted total of the six indicators → add the net Flexible Adjustment → determine the level against your city's lines → apply the Red Line cap (the final hard constraint).
rules.flex.no_double_title: Penalty boundary: nothing is penalised twice
rules.flex.no_double_body: Penalties apply only to misconduct the six indicators cannot capture. The following already have their own mechanism and are not penalised again:
rules.incentive.rate_none: Levels B / C: no cash incentive
rules.incentive.basis: Paid per Perfect Order, together with the weekly invoice. Perfect Order definition: official DETA + 1 minute (from 2026-07-27).
rules.incentive.redline_note: The month's incentive is cancelled if the Debt Red Line is triggered (see the Red Line rules).
rules.protection.exempt: The {months} consecutive calendar months from your starting month are the new-vendor protection period: you are rated normally and enjoy your level's benefits normally, and a level C within this period neither triggers the termination process nor counts toward its tally.
rules.protection.counted: From month {month} onward, a level C starts counting toward the termination tally.
rules.protection.cutoff: Starting-month rule (cut-off on day {day}): if your first order was on or before day {day}, that same month counts as month 1; if it was after day {day}, month 1 is the following month. Day {day} itself counts as "≤ {day}".
rules.protection.redline_exception: One exception: the Debt Red Line applies from your first billing cycle — payment discipline has no grace period.
rules.protection.no_ceiling: If your first assessment after the protection period reaches A or S, that actual level is awarded: there is no "new vendors cap at B" ceiling.
rules.clearance.body: Counting from month {start}, {months} consecutive calendar months at level C → the partnership termination process begins. Months at C within the exempt period do not count toward the tally. Your Regional Manager (RM) will inform you separately of the specifics.
rules.benefits.note: These benefits match the official announcement materials.
rules.benefits.cash.title: Cash rewards — the most direct return
rules.benefits.cash.b1: Level S: {sRate} per Perfect Order; level A: {aRate} per Perfect Order
rules.benefits.cash.b2: Paid with the weekly invoice, capped at {cap} per vendor per month
rules.benefits.cash.b3: The month's reward is cancelled if the Debt Red Line is triggered

rules.benefits.growth.b1: New-city eligibility: opening stations in new cities is open to levels S and A only
rules.benefits.growth.b2: Sign-up fee waiver: earn level S in a month and you can open a new city the following month without the 50,000-peso sign-up fee (valid the following month only, not carried over)
rules.benefits.growth.b3: Rider lead referrals: rider sign-up leads go first to higher-level partners
rules.benefits.growth.b4: Priority on new business: pilots of DiDi's new business lines invite level S and A partners first
rules.benefits.honor.title: Recognition — your strongest card for recruiting riders
rules.benefits.honor.b1: Monthly official level S certificate: DiDi-certified, to display at your station
rules.benefits.honor.b2: Level shown in the rider app: every rider knows their vendor's level

changelog.v6.credit_replaces_flex: The Repayment Credit (20%) replaces the former flexibility floor component; no debt means automatic full marks
changelog.v6.redline_added: Debt Red Line added: a weekly mark line plus a monthly trigger condition; once triggered, the month's cash incentive is forfeited
changelog.v6.ontime_to_slot: On-time rate assessment replaced by the Slot Compliance Rate (25%, monthly average excluding surge)
changelog.v6.city_lines: The A and C lines are set per city (CDMX / MTY); the S line and the scale threshold are the same across the market
changelog.v6.newrider_curp: The New Rider Ratio uses the CURP-verified "entirely new to the industry" definition (5%)
changelog.v6.reason: Comprehensive upgrade of the level system: from growth-driven to all-round development (finalised 2026-08-12)
changelog.v6a.redline_cap: In the month the Red Line is triggered, the level is capped at B (matching the official announcement)
changelog.v6a.protection_rated: During the protection period vendors are rated normally and receive benefits normally; the exemption applies only to the termination tally
changelog.v6a.flex: Flexible Adjustment mechanism added: the platform may add or subtract up to 10 points on top of the month's total
changelog.v6a.orders_perfect: The order indicator is unified to Perfect Orders: average daily Perfect Orders (July's demo data uses completed orders; the tier outcome is identical)
changelog.v6a.reason: Four definitions aligned with the official vendor announcement (operations decision, 2026-08-13)
changelog.v6b.flex_split: Flexible Adjustment split out: the activity bonus and the violation penalty are defined and displayed separately, with a net cap of ±10. Why: the bonus is an incentive published in advance that vendors actively earn, while the penalty is punishment determined after the fact — different in nature, so they cannot be merged into a single net figure. It also makes explicit that the penalty does not stack with the Repayment Credit or the Red Line.
changelog.v6b.orders_caliber: The definition of average daily Perfect Orders is pinned down: total Perfect Orders in the period ÷ days in the period (calendar days for a month, 7 days for a week). Why: to use the same definition as the official announcement and the cash incentive, and to end the mixing of completed orders and Perfect Orders.
changelog.v6b.d3r_naming: The service-quality indicator is published to vendors under a single name, D-3R%; the tiers <1 / 1–2 / 2–3 / ≥3 are unchanged. Why: historical materials used three names (3R, D-duty 2R%, D-3R%); they are unified to the official announcement.
changelog.v6b.blocked_rider: The Account Compliance Rate definition is fixed: riders blocked this month by the anti-fraud red line (deduplicated) ÷ riders completing orders this month. Why: fixing both the numerator's criteria and the denominator prevents the definition from drifting.
changelog.v6b.newrider_real: The New Rider Ratio switches to real CURP data (riders entirely new to the industry ÷ riders completing orders), retiring the proxy definition based on the February–July cumulative monthly average. Why: the real data is now connected and the proxy has served its purpose.
changelog.v6b.credit_unlock: The Repayment Credit is recalculated from two components (share overdue >7 days at 60%, bad-debt share at 40%) on each weekly snapshot. Why: both component values can now be obtained from the overdue detail, so the score goes from a read-only input to something recalculable and simulable.
changelog.v6b.reason: Definitions finalised (2026-08-13): every indicator's definition, name and data source matches the official vendor announcement, removing historical ambiguity.
changelog.cr0814.summary: Level system adjustment (effective 2026-09): the scale threshold is removed, score lines are redefined per city, and four definitions are refined
changelog.cr0814.drop_s_gate: The level S scale threshold is removed (previously required ≥1,250 average daily Perfect Orders): level S now depends on total points alone. Why: the threshold was too harsh for mid-to-large vendors, who could not clear it no matter how hard they tried, so it lost its motivating purpose — those vendors now have a route to S again.
changelog.cr0814.s_by_city: The level S line is now set per city (previously ≥80 nationwide): CDMX ≥80, MTY ≥85. Why: the two cities sit at different score levels, and a single standard would leave one of them with clearly too many or too few S vendors.
changelog.cr0814.lines_recalibrated: The A and C lines are recalibrated for the new definitions: CDMX A ≥45, MTY A ≥65, and a C line of <15 in both cities. Why: the refined definitions shift total points down overall, and keeping the old lines would push the S+A share and the number of C vendors far from target; the new lines correspond to an S+A share of roughly 30% in both cities.
changelog.cr0814.credit_overdue_only: The Repayment Credit now looks only at the share overdue >7 days; the bad-debt share no longer enters the calculation. Why: both reflect the same thing (whether debt is cleared on time), so combining them penalised the same problem twice and was hard to explain to vendors.
changelog.cr0814.slot_daily: The Slot Compliance Rate is now accumulated daily: slots met each day of the month ÷ total target slots for the month (previously the average of weekly rates). Why: daily accumulation reflects actual compliance across the whole month, whereas a weekly average gave equal weight to weeks with many and with few shifts.
changelog.cr0814.newrider_denominator: The New Rider Ratio's denominator becomes "riders hired this month" (previously riders completing orders), and the tiers adjust to ≥70% / 50% / 30%. Why: the focus shifts from recruiting volume to recruiting quality — how many of your new hires are new to the industry.
changelog.cr0814.natural_month: The assessment window is aligned to the calendar month (July = 7/1–7/31, for example). Why: some indicators previously used the invoice's 5-week window (35 days spanning two months), which contradicted the rule of assessing by calendar month and made reconciliation harder for vendors.
changelog.cr0814.reason: Six points raised in the 2026-08-13 review with management, confirmed on 2026-08-14 (change order CR-20260814). Effective from the first official assessment in 2026-09; August is a transition period.
changelog.a10.summary: Repayment Credit: full marks are reserved for having no overdue debt (CR-20260814 A10)
changelog.a10.reason: Unify the Repayment Credit's full-marks standard: full marks mean no overdue debt, not a low enough overdue share (management's definition, 2026-08-14).

admin.editor.readonly_online: The online console does not edit rules directly. The single source of truth is data/rules.json — follow the «change order → local execution → regression suite → re-import» flow so the database and the repository cannot diverge. Simulation and the sandbox on this page work as usual.
admin.history.local_only: Version backups live in the local rules_history/ folder and are not visible online. Rollback also follows the change-order flow.
admin.online_note: Online mode: simulation, the sandbox and data browsing work as usual; saving and rolling back rules is disabled — data/rules.json is the single source of truth and changes are re-imported after going through the change-order flow.
